title: Desktop check: a multiplayer GOB hosted by OpenJKDF2's -autostart -mp
body: Found while choosing the listing's screenshots (2026-10-29): for OpenJKDF2, Gobinator adds -autostart -sp -episode <GOB> -map <first level> whatever the episode's TYPE (src/launch.cpp, AddAutostart). Some of the studio's own public GOBs are multiplayer episodes (TYPE 2 in episode.jk): COG Factory's Foosball Stadium (P83.GOB) and SM HQ (SMHQ.GOB). Whether -sp loads such a level sensibly, or whether Gobinator should skip the autostart for TYPE 2 and leave the episode at the top of the multiplayer list, is untested. A headless check with the harness first; no window needed.

log.text: Source read (2026-10-29): upstream OpenJKDF2 can autostart multiplayer. Main.c's command line takes -mp / -multiplayer beside -sp (shinyquagsire23, e4cc2005, 2023-10-11, the same commit as -autostart), and both test builds (v0.9.8, v0.9.9) carry the strings. Without -sp, Main_StartupDedicated hosts a session on this PC (sithMulti_CreatePlayer) and loads -episode/-map into it, the local player playing (jkGuiNetHost_bIsDedicated stays 0; only -dedicatedServer sets it). Caveats in upstream's code: the host plays a stand-in character (ky.3do, green saber, jediRank 0, the "Fake player" block), not the player's .mpc; the host settings are the player's last Host Game ones (registry: name, max players, limits, teams, port), and the session is always flagged SESSIONFLAG_ISDEDICATED (shown as dedicated in other players' join list). The fork's libretro build already picks SP or MP from the episode's TYPE (jkSession_ResolveAutoBootMode) and resolves the profile's MP character. Untested on the stock desktop build: that needs a game window (the user's go).

Done in 0e2534b (the user's rulings, docs/DECISIONS.md 2026-10-29): TYPE 1 -> -autostart -sp, TYPE 2 -> -autostart -mp (hosted on this PC), any other TYPE (CTF 8 included) -> the menu; a GOB with no episode.jk (a mod) or one that cannot be read is left where it is and JK starts at its menu. Unit tests and run-v11-scenarios.ps1 (R5, R6, U, U2; 200 checks) pass. Headless: the libretro core booted SM HQ (TYPE 2) as a hosted game into smhq.jkl. Left for the user at the keyboard: one desktop run of a multiplayer GOB on the stock OpenJKDF2 (v0.9.9 test copy), to see the stand-in character, the Host Game settings and any firewall prompt.
updated: title, labels +needs-user-test

done: The user ran it on 2026-10-29 ("1-3 works"): the build from 0e2534b beside stock OpenJKDF2 v0.9.9 (testinstall/openjkdf2-v099, the shipping ini, nothing set), GOBs dragged onto gobinator.exe. P71.GOB (The Crab Factory, TYPE 1) landed in its level; SMHQ.gob (SM HQ, TYPE 2) hosted a game and reached the level through -autostart -mp; Sith Sabers.gob (a mod, no episode.jk) opened the game at its menu and stayed where it was. Checked afterwards: gobinator.log (mod noted, no autostart), Episode (P71.GOB, SMHQ.gob, only the SMHQ folder), mod emptied of the older build's recorded P03 copy, OpenJKDF2's registry.json serverEpisodeGob=SMHQ / serverMapJkl=smhq.jkl. The character played and any firewall prompt were not reported. Capture the Flag still opens at the menu (DECISIONS 2026-10-29).

The user, 2026-10-29: in SM HQ they spawned as Kyle Katarn, the default (upstream's stand-in, as read in Main_StartupDedicated); Windows Firewall asked once and they allowed it (README now says so). A Capture the Flag episode opened at OpenJKDF2's main menu, as decided. title: Ask for the JK folder when none is found beside gobinator.exe (first-run folder picker)
body:
Today, when gobinator.exe is not in a JK folder and gobinator.ini sets no JK_FOLDER, a double-clicked GOB ends in a message box: "No JK program was found in <folder>. Gobinator looks for inject.exe (with jkgm.json), openjkdf2-64.exe, JediKnight.exe and JK.EXE. Put gobinator.exe and gobinator.ini in your JK folder, or set JK_FOLDER or JK_EXECUTABLE in gobinator.ini." Without the ini at all: "gobinator.ini was not found beside gobinator.exe." Nothing is changed on disk either way (scenario 13 and 14 in docs/BETA-1-TESTS.md).

The user asked (2026-10-30), preparing new-user tests of beta 1, whether a new user sees a prompt asking where their JK folder is, as Anarchy Arcade's core does with its first-run welcome.

Proposal, for the user to rule on: on that path, open Windows' folder picker (IFileOpenDialog with FOS_PICKFOLDERS, titled "Where is your Jedi Knight folder?"), check the chosen folder holds a JK program, write JK_FOLDER = <it> into gobinator.ini (creating the ini from the package's text when it is missing), and carry on with the GOB. Cancel keeps today's message. Then "unzip anywhere, Open with gobinator.exe" works, and the README's step 1 becomes optional. Small: one dialog and an ini write; the scenario harness can cover the write with GOBINATOR_NO_MESSAGES plus an environment variable naming the folder the picker would return.

title: Warn when a Steam JK folder is not the one Steam starts
body: Steam's JediKnight.exe hands any start to Steam, which runs the install Steam has registered (HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\LucasArts Entertainment Company\JediKnight\1.0 'Install Path', written by Steam's install script), with the same switches. If Gobinator sits in another Steam JK folder (the user has two: the registered, patched 'Star Wars Jedi Knight' and a copied 'Star Wars Jedi Knight Vanilla'), it copies the GOB into that folder's mod, while the game Steam starts reads the registered folder's mod: the episode is missing, with no error. Options: warn in the message/log when the JK folder (JediKnight.exe kind) differs from Steam's registered path; or copy into the registered folder's mod instead. Measured 2026-10-27 (gob-4xp6).

log.text: done: Built (the user's pick 2026-10-27: warn and stop, docs/DECISIONS.md). Before touching the mod folder, Gobinator checks whether the program is Steam's DRM'd EXE (IsSteamStub: a PE section named .bind, which Steam's JediKnight.EXE, JK Remastered v1.0's JediKnight.EXE and MotS's JediKnightM.EXE carry; the user's community-patched JediKnight.EXE has none and runs where it is). If so, and Steam's registered install (Install Path in HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\LucasArts Entertainment Company\JediKnight\1.0, read through the 32-bit view) is another folder (SameFolder: by volume and file ID, so links and spellings do not matter), it copies nothing, starts nothing, and the message and log name the folder Steam starts and say to put Gobinator there or set JK_FOLDER. With no registered install it goes on and logs a note. Checked read-only with gobinator-tests --detect: the Steam vanilla folder and its copy are refused (Steam starts ...\Star Wars Jedi Knight); the registered patched folder is not Steam's DRM. Unit tests for IsSteamStub (hand-built PE headers, and fakesteamjk.exe, a build of fakejk.c with a .bind section) and SameFolder; new scenario T in run-v11-scenarios.ps1 (23 scenarios, all pass).

title: Pass OpenJKDF2 only the switches its EXE knows
body: OpenJKDF2 quits with 'Error in arguments' on a switch it does not know (Main.c:758-761). Gobinator adds -autostart -sp -episode -map to any OpenJKDF2, and -doNotResumeLast when aarcadecore.dll is beside it. Upstream added -autostart in 2023-10; JK Remastered 3.3 reportedly ships OpenJKDF2 0.9.1 (ModDB snippets, 2026-10-27), which may predate it, so a double-click there could start the game and have it quit at once. Fix: read the EXE and add each switch only when its string is in it (a NUL-delimited '-autostart', '-doNotResumeLast' as stored in the EXE: how v0.9.8 was checked on 2026-10-27, which found -autostart but not -doNotResumeLast). Replaces the aarcadecore guess. Test: fake EXEs with and without the strings.

log.text: Checked 2026-10-27: JK Remastered 3.3's openjkdf2-64.exe is v0.9.1 and its EXE contains -autostart, -sp, -episode, -map, -path, -devMode but not -doNotResumeLast. So JKR 3.3 does not quit on Gobinator's autostart; the fix still matters for older builds and for exact switch sets. A copy of JKR 3.3 vanilla is the real test case.

done: AddAutostart (src/launch.cpp) now reads the OpenJKDF2 EXE and collects the switches it holds as strings of their own (KnownSwitches: a NUL before and after, any case, the way OpenJKDF2 keeps them). It adds -autostart -sp -episode -map only when all four are there, and -doNotResumeLast only when the EXE has it, which replaces the aarcadecore.dll guess. An OpenJKDF2 without them (before v0.9.1, the first tag with -autostart) is started at its menu instead of quitting with 'Error in arguments', and the log says why. Checked read-only with gobinator-tests --detect, which now prints these switches: v0.9.1 (JKR 3.3 vanilla, and the backup in the play folder), v0.9.8 and v0.9.9 (test copies, and the play folder) know the four but not -doNotResumeLast; only the user's fork build has it. Unit tests: KnownSwitches, plus AddAutostart on fake EXEs (upstream, fork, pre-0.9.1, a partial set, an unreadable EXE). run-v11-scenarios.ps1: 22 scenarios all pass, with new R2 (an old OpenJKDF2 gets no autostart) and R3 (the fork gets -doNotResumeLast); its fake OpenJKDF2 carries the strings after its image. run-openjkdf2-boot.ps1 passes. Both scripts wait with WaitForExit, not -Wait.

title: An OpenJKDF2 test install for Gobinator
body: The development bed (the user, 2026-10-27). title: Straight into a Capture the Flag episode: OpenJKDF2 hosts from the command line without team flags
body:
The user's beta run of 2026-10-30 12:14 (play folder log): StarDestroyer.gob ("Imperial Star Destroyer", TYPE 8, first level jkedit.jkl) was copied, listed first and OpenJKDF2 opened at its menu, as decided on 2026-10-29 (CTF at the menu until a desktop check shows command-line hosting sets CTF up right). The user expected to land in the multiplayer session.

What OpenJKDF2's source says about that check (the user's checkout of upstream, src/Main/Main.c Main_StartupDedicated and src/Gui/jkGuiNetHost.c): the command-line host (-autostart -mp -episode X -map Y) takes its game flags from the saved Host Game settings as they are (registry.json: gameFlags 144, bIsTeams false on the user's install). Only the Host Game screen adds the team flags (MULTIMODEFLAG_TEAMS | 0x2 | 0x100), and only when its Team mode box is ticked; nothing keys off the episode being CTF (JK_EPISODE_SPECIAL_CTF). So a CTF episode hosted from the command line today would run without teams unless the player's last Host Game had Team mode on, and then every deathmatch autostart would have teams too.

Options for the user:
1. Keep CTF at the menu (today). The episode is first in the list; Host Game with Team mode ticked is two clicks.
2. Gobinator sends -autostart -mp for TYPE 8 as for deathmatch, accepting that teams follow the saved Team mode setting. Cheap, but wrong whenever that box was last off.
3. Ask OpenJKDF2 (the aaopenjkdf2 fork, or upstream) to host a TYPE 8 episode with the team flags when started from the command line, or to take a switch for it (-teams); Gobinator then sends -mp for CTF when the EXE knows that switch (as it detects -doNotResumeLast). The play folder's openjkdf2-64.exe is an upstream-style build (no -doNotResumeLast), so the fork would have to be the one played, or the change go upstream.

done: No change (the user, 2026-10-30: "Oh I didn't know it was a CTF map. That is correct behavior for CTF, so no change needed."). CTF episodes stay first in the list with OpenJKDF2 at its menu, which the Host Game screen's Team mode box then sets up right; the source shows command-line hosting would run them without teams. Recorded in docs/DECISIONS.md.
